layer.description: The polygon data set represents the information gathered from the legal description on deeds, lot layout of recorded plats, declaration of condominium documents, recorded and unrecorded surveys. This information is continually updated. The dataset extends countywide

coverage.note: All 67 DOR county numbers (11-77) present plus CO_NO 0 for unjoined polygons. Service description: each county omits confidential records subject to redaction under Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, so redacted parcels can be absent.

identity.why: CO_NO + PARCEL_ID is the DOR tax-roll key; PARCEL_ID formats are county-specific. PARCELNO (polygon parcel number) equals PARCEL_ID on joined rows but has no county number on unjoined rows (CO_NO 0), so it cannot be made statewide-unique. STATE_PAR_, ALT_KEY and OID_ repeat exactly like PARCEL_ID. No GlobalID exists.
identity.exclusion: attributeExclusions CO_NO [0] and PARCEL_ID [' '] (the same 97,244 unjoined rows).

uniqueness.result: PARCEL_ID repeats with distinct geometry (23 values in the Tampa bbox, 2,000+ in Hillsborough); parts are mostly disjoint but some overlap slightly (max 0.79 m2 in Hillsborough 1927179SI000000C00000U, 86 rows). nativeGeometryMode parts without disjointParts. The one statewide-sample repeat outside the Tampa bbox was in the same county (a multi-part parcel).

denseCellTiming: A 0.003 degree Tampa cell returned 64 parcels from 116 rows in 16.3 s over 6 requests (slowest 3.4 s). The 0.001 degree verification cells took 18-21 s; single requests up to 6 s.
caveats: PARCEL_ID is county-scoped, so identity is the reversible composite CO_NO~PARCEL_ID.

Many roll parcels are stored as several polygon rows (e.g. 86 rows for one Hillsborough condominium parcel); all components are fetched and unioned. Some components overlap slightly (largest observed 0.79 m2), so overlap is not rejected for this provider.
The layer carries owner, address and sale columns; only CO_NO, PARCEL_ID and OBJECTID are requested.
Statewide envelope queries are slow (about 11 s for a 0.01 degree box, 18 s for 46 object IDs); small cells are required.
